exposure: first wheezing episode before 1 year of age
outcome: development of asthma in school ages
finding: Clinical features, such as early first wheezing episode, preterm birth, and cesarean delivery, were more valuable than serum periostin, YKL-40, and osteopontin biomarkers in predicting the development of asthma in school-age years in children who had recurrent wheezing in the pre-school-age period.
mod_finding: Cesarean section delivery was associated with an increased risk of developing asthma in school age.
